checks.note: Authorization page lists internal connection tokens, PATs (static, act as user) and OAuth 2.0 for scoped/public integrations. Internal connections require a workspace owner.

Request-limits page gives rate limits (180/min, 600/min for Business/Enterprise, ~3 req/s data source queries) but states no plan requirement. Free-plan access rests on search snippets and an old 2021 changelog, with no current plan matrix. A newer changelog says Free workspace block limits now apply to internal connections via the REST API (effective Sept 8, 2026), which I did not verify. Keep self_serve_free at low confidence.

Intro page describes HTTPS/JSON requests to api.notion.com, so REST is a fair inference, and names pages, databases, users and file uploads. The page names no API style and no full endpoint list. 'Broad' is a reasonable judgment, not a stated fact.
Notion's MCP guide calls it a 'hosted, actively maintained server' at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, so it is official.

ready_with_caveats follows from the other fields. The caveats listed (rate limits, owner-created internal tokens, unconfirmed free-plan access) are accurate. The Free block-limit change is a further caveat.

corrected.one_liner: Notion is a connected workspace for notes, documents, wikis, and databases/projects.
corrected.auth_notes: Internal connection API token (static, per-workspace, created by a workspace owner) and personal access tokens (static, acts with the user's permissions), both sent as Authorization: Bearer with a Notion-Version header. OAuth 2.0 for public/scoped integrations (code exchange for access and refresh tokens).
corrected.access_notes: The API docs name no plan requirement. Internal tokens require a workspace owner to create the connection. Free-plan API access is inferred, not stated on the cited page. A Notion help page snippet and an old 2021 changelog suggest Free workspaces can use the API, and a newer changelog says Free workspace block limits are enforced for internal connections (effective Sept 8, 2026; not verified). Rate limit is 180 req/min per connection on non-Business/Enterprise plans, 600 req/min on Business/Enterprise. Data source queries are about 3 req/s. Whether PATs need admin approval is unclear.
corrected.blocker: Rate limits (180 req/min on lower plans, about 3 req/s for data source queries). Internal tokens require a workspace owner. Free-plan API access is not explicitly confirmed, and Free workspace block limits may apply. The 'broad' rating is based on the named resources (pages, databases, users, file uploads), not a full endpoint list.
